examples.ko: 인사과 직원이 급여 명세서를 메일로 보내 줬어요.
examples.en: A staff member in HR emailed me my pay statement.
There is a payment I don't recognize on my card statement.

examples.ko: 승급 심사 결과는 다음 달 급여 명세서에 반영돼요.
examples.en: The promotion review result will be reflected in next month's pay statement.
Please check your phone bill statement.
Looking at the statement, a lot was taken out for taxes.
I got an itemized medical bill from the hospital.

explain: 돈이 어디에 얼마 쓰였는지 항목별로 적은 문서예요. 영수증이 '냈다'는 증명이라면, 명세서는 안에 든 내용을 자세히 보여 줘요. '급여 명세서', '카드 명세서'처럼 앞에 종류를 붙여서 써요.

phrases.en: I checked the statement to see if the amount was right.
phrases.nuance_ko: 항목별 내용이 맞는지 살펴볼 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing for checking whether itemized details are correct.

phrases.en: I received this month's statement by email.
phrases.nuance_ko: 우편이나 메일로 문서를 받는다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means receiving the document by mail or email.

phrases.en: On the phone bill statement, the charge went up.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞에 종류를 붙여서 어떤 비용의 명세서인지 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A type goes before 'myeongseseo' to say which charges it covers.

explain_en: This is a document that lists, item by item, where money went and how much. A receipt proves you paid, while a 명세서 shows the details inside. Put the type in front, as in '급여 명세서' (pay statement) and '카드 명세서' (card statement).

examples.ko: 그 선수의 몸값이 작년보다 두 배 올랐어요.
examples.en: That player's market value doubled compared to last year.

examples.ko: 몸값 높은 배우를 쓰면 제작비가 올라가요.
examples.en: Hiring a high-priced actor raises the production cost.

examples.ko: 저는 제 몸값을 올리려고 자격증을 땄어요.
examples.en: I got a certificate to raise my own market value.

examples.ko: 축구 선수 몸값은 나이가 들면 내려가요.
examples.en: A soccer player's value drops as they get older.

examples.ko: 범인이 사람을 잡아 놓고 몸값을 요구했어요.
examples.en: The criminal took a person and demanded a ransom.
He couldn't change teams because of his price.

explain: 연예인, 선수, 회사원이 시장에서 얼마의 가치로 평가받는지를 돈에 비유해서 말해요. '연봉'은 실제로 받는 돈이고, 몸값은 사람의 가치를 말하는 느낌이 강해요. 인질을 풀어 주는 대가로 내는 돈도 몸값이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 드라마가 인기를 얻은 뒤 몸값이 올랐어요.
phrases.en: That actor's market value went up after the drama became popular.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인기나 실력 때문에 사람의 가치가 높아졌을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person's value rises due to popularity or skill.

phrases.en: A player with a high market value also earns a big salary.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시장에서 비싸게 평가받는 사람을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a person who is rated highly in the market.

phrases.en: The criminal demanded a ransom.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 풀어 주는 대가로 돈을 달라고 할 때 쓰는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ransom meaning: asking for money in exchange for releasing a person.

explain_en: It describes, in terms of money, how much a celebrity, athlete, or worker is valued on the market. 연봉 is the pay actually received, while 몸값 feels more like the person's worth. The money paid to free a hostage is also called 몸값.

examples.en: Our company trades with many countries.
Korea has traded with China for a long time.
People who trade check the exchange rate often.
To trade with other countries, you need many documents.
Price matters when you trade rice.
I decided which goods I want to trade.

explain: 나라 사이에 물건을 사고팔 때 써요. 보통 '무역을 하다'로 말해요. 내보내는 것은 '수출', 들여오는 것은 '수입'이에요.

phrases.example: 그 나라는 여러 나라와 무역을 해요.
phrases.en: That country trades with many countries.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무역하다'와 같은 뜻이고 보통 이렇게 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '무역하다', and this is the usual way to say it.

phrases.en: I work at a trading company.
phrases.nuance_ko: '무역' 뒤에 '회사'를 붙여 일하는 곳을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Put '회사' after '무역' to name a workplace.

phrases.example: 두 나라는 오래전부터 서로 무역하고 있어요.
phrases.en: The two countries have traded with each other for a long time.
phrases.nuance_ko: 무역이 계속 이어지고 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the trade is ongoing.

explain_en: Use it for buying and selling goods between countries. People usually say '무역을 하다'. Sending goods out is '수출', bringing them in is '수입'.

dis.h: buy and sell goods between countries

p.n: Same meaning; 교역하다 sounds more formal.

en: being unsold in presale; unsold home

examples.en: They say unsold apartments have increased in the new town.
When there are many unsold units, construction companies struggle.

examples.ko: 정부가 미분양을 줄이기 위해 대책을 내놨어요.
examples.en: The government announced measures to reduce unsold homes.

examples.ko: 미분양에 대한 걱정 때문에 분양을 미루는 회사도 있어요.
examples.en: Some companies postpone sales out of worry about unsold units.
Unsold homes in this area have decreased compared to last year.

examples.ko: 계약자가 없어서 미분양으로 남은 집이 많아요.
examples.en: Many homes remain unsold because no one signed a contract.

explain: 새로 지은 아파트를 분양했는데 다 팔리지 않고 남은 상태나 그 집을 말해요. 주로 부동산 뉴스에서 '미분양 아파트', '미분양 물량'처럼 나와요. 중고 집이 안 팔리는 경우에는 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.example: 이 지역에는 미분양 아파트가 아직 남아 있어요.
phrases.en: There are still unsold new apartments in this area.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분양했는데 팔리지 않은 새 아파트를 말할 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for new apartments that were offered but not sold.

phrases.en: I hear the amount of unsold units is decreasing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔리지 않고 남은 집의 전체 수량을 말할 때 뉴스에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the news for the total number of unsold units.

phrases.en: When housing prices fall, unsold homes increase.
phrases.nuance_ko: 팔리지 않는 새집이 많아지는 상황을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a situation where more new homes remain unsold.

explain_en: It refers to the state of newly built apartments that were put up for sale but not all sold, or to those leftover homes. It appears mostly in real estate news, as in '미분양 아파트' and '미분양 물량'. It isn't used for second-hand homes that fail to sell.

examples.en: This expressway was built with private capital.

examples.ko: 민자 도로는 통행료가 더 비쌀 때가 많아요.
examples.en: Toll fees on private-investment roads are often higher.

examples.ko: 시는 민자를 유치해서 새 경기장을 지을 계획이에요.
examples.en: The city plans to attract private investment and build a new stadium.

examples.ko: 정부 예산이 부족하면 민자 사업을 추진하기도 해요.
examples.en: When the government budget is short, they sometimes pursue private-investment projects.

examples.ko: 민자 터널은 요금을 따로 내야 해요.
examples.en: For a privately funded tunnel, you have to pay a separate fee.
Attracting private investment was delayed, so construction was postponed.

explain: '민간 자본'을 줄인 말이에요. 도로, 철도, 경기장처럼 원래 나라가 짓는 시설을 민간 돈으로 지을 때 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 나라 돈으로 짓는 것은 '재정 사업'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: A new airport railway was built as a private investment project.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민간 돈으로 시설을 짓는 사업을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A project that builds facilities with private money.

phrases.example: 시는 민자 유치로 경기장을 지으려고 해요.
phrases.en: The city plans to build a stadium by attracting private investment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 민간 돈을 끌어오는 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for bringing in private money.

phrases.en: They gathered private capital and built a bridge.
phrases.nuance_ko: '민자'의 원래 형태이고, 풀어 쓴 말이라 뜻이 더 분명해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 민자; spelled out, its meaning is clearer.

explain_en: It is a shortened form of '민간 자본' (private capital). It often appears in the news when facilities the state would normally build, such as roads, railways and stadiums, are built with private money. Projects built with state money are called '재정 사업'.

examples.ko: 하향 곡선을 그리던 판매량이 이번 달에 겨우 반등했어요.
examples.en: Sales that had been on a downward curve finally rebounded this month.

examples.ko: 매출이 반등할 조짐이 있어요? 아직 확실하지는 않지만 주문이 조금 늘었어요.
examples.en: Are there signs that sales will rebound? It's not certain yet, but orders have increased a little.

examples.ko: 어제 크게 떨어진 주가가 오늘은 반등하기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The stock price that fell sharply yesterday started to rebound today.

examples.ko: 환율이 반등하면 여행 계획을 다시 생각해 봐야 해요.
examples.en: If the exchange rate rebounds, we'll have to rethink our travel plans.

examples.ko: 경기가 반등하려면 신제품이 먼저 나와야 해요.
examples.en: For business to rebound, new products have to come out first.
My grades dropped but rebounded on the final exam, so I'm happy.

explain: 한동안 내려가던 것이 다시 올라갈 때 써요. 주가, 매출, 환율, 성적 이야기에 어울리고, 처음부터 오르는 것에는 그냥 '오르다'를 써요.

phrases.en: Stock prices started to rebound.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내려가던 것이 오르기 시작하는 때를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Marks the moment something starts rising after a fall.

phrases.en: After the stock price rebounded, it fell again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 오른 다음에 일어난 일을 이어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to connect what happened after the rebound.

phrases.en: Sales will rebound next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 오를 것을 예상할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to predict a future rise.

explain_en: Used when something that had been falling for a while goes back up. It suits talk about stock prices, sales, exchange rates and grades. For something that simply rises from the start, just use '오르다'.

examples.ko: 정부는 내년 방위비를 조금 늘리기로 했어요.
examples.en: The government decided to raise next year's defense spending a little.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 방위비 분담금 이야기를 계속 해요.
examples.en: The news keeps talking about the defense cost-sharing money.

examples.ko: 방위비가 늘어나면 다른 예산이 줄 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If defense spending increases, other budgets may shrink.
The amount of money spent on defense is different in each country.
They debated the defense spending issue in the National Assembly.

examples.ko: 방위비 때문에 복지 예산이 부족하다는 의견도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people say the welfare budget is short because of defense spending.

explain: '국방비'나 '국방 예산'과 비슷하지만, 뉴스에서는 '방위비 분담금'처럼 외국 군대와 관련된 비용 이야기에서 자주 나와요. '늘리다, 줄이다, 분담하다' 같은 말과 함께 써요.

phrases.en: Each country has a different reason for increasing its defense spending.
phrases.nuance_ko: '늘리다, 줄이다'와 함께 예산의 변화를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 늘리다 or 줄이다 to talk about changes in the budget.

phrases.example: 방위비 분담금을 얼마나 낼지 두 나라가 이야기했어요.
phrases.en: The two countries discussed how much to pay for the defense cost-sharing.
phrases.nuance_ko: 외국 군대와 관련해 나눠 내는 돈을 말하는 뉴스 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news term for money shared in connection with foreign troops.

phrases.example: 국방비는 나라 예산에서 큰 부분을 차지해요.
phrases.en: Defense spending takes up a big part of the national budget.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방위비와 비슷하지만 외국 군대 이야기가 없을 때도 널리 쓰는 일반적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Close in meaning, but a more general term used even when foreign troops aren't involved.

explain_en: It is similar to '국방비' or '국방 예산' (defense budget), but in the news it often appears in '방위비 분담금' (defense cost-sharing) topics about foreign troops. It goes with verbs like '늘리다', '줄이다' and '분담하다'.

examples.en: When you eat with a friend, the fun doubles.
If you keep making an effort, the effect will multiply.
It even rained, so my fatigue got much worse.

examples.ko: 마음이 맞는 사람과 일하면 재미가 배가되는 것 같아요.
examples.en: Working with someone who clicks with me seems to double the fun.

examples.ko: 여행은 좋은 사람과 함께하면 기쁨이 배가되잖아요.
examples.en: A trip is more enjoyable when you share it with good people, right?

examples.ko: 걱정이 배가되어 밤새 잠을 잘 못 잤어요.
examples.en: My worries multiplied, so I hardly slept all night.

explain: 정확히 두 배라기보다 기쁨, 슬픔, 효과, 재미, 걱정이 훨씬 커질 때 자주 써요. 숫자가 실제로 두 배가 될 때는 '두 배로 늘다'가 더 자연스러워요. '배가'의 '배'는 '배가 고프다'의 배(몸)와 달라요.

phrases.example: 좋은 소식을 함께 나누니 기쁨이 배가됐어요.
phrases.en: Sharing the good news together doubled our joy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기쁨, 재미처럼 마음의 느낌이 훨씬 커질 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a feeling like joy or fun grows much bigger.

phrases.example: 운동과 식단을 함께 하면 효과가 배가돼요.
phrases.en: Combining exercise and diet doubles the effect.
phrases.nuance_ko: 두 가지를 함께 할 때 효과가 훨씬 커진다고 말할 때 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Fits when two things together make the effect much greater.

phrases.en: The number of customers doubled this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 숫자가 실제로 두 배가 될 때는 배가되다보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than 배가되다 when a number really does double.

explain_en: Rather than meaning exactly twice, it is often used when joy, sadness, effects, fun or worries grow a lot. When a number really becomes twice as large, '두 배로 늘다' sounds more natural. The '배' in '배가' is different from the '배' (belly) in '배가 고프다'.

examples.ko: 주식이 있으면 배당금을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you own stock, you can receive dividends.
Dividends increased this year compared to last year.
The timing of dividends differs from company to company.
I ate out with my family using the dividend I received.
I bought this stock because of the dividends.
I did not know that tax is charged on dividends too.

explain: 주식, 투자와 함께 나오고 '배당금을 받다/지급하다'처럼 써요. 줄여서 그냥 '배당'이라고도 해요. 예금이나 대출에 붙는 '이자'와는 달라요.

phrases.en: I receive dividends from the company at the end of every year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주식을 가진 사람 입장에서 가장 흔히 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase from a shareholder's point of view.

phrases.en: That company paid dividends to its shareholders.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사 입장에서 돈을 내줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the company's side when it pays out the money.

phrases.en: This company is famous for its high dividends.
phrases.nuance_ko: '배당금'을 줄여서 편하게 부르는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shortened, casual way of saying 배당금.

explain_en: It comes up with stocks and investing, in phrases like '배당금을 받다/지급하다'. It is often shortened to just '배당'. It differs from '이자' (interest), which is attached to savings and loans.

examples.en: That company brought in a lot of money last year.
It is a country that earns foreign currency through exports.
How much does the shop bring in per day these days?

examples.ko: 이 가게가 한 해에 벌어들인 돈이 꽤 많대요.
examples.en: I heard this shop earned quite a lot in a year.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 수출로 더 많은 돈을 벌어들여야 해요.
examples.en: This country has to earn more money through exports.

examples.ko: 그 가게는 연휴에 돈을 더 벌어들이려고 밤늦게까지 문을 열었어요.
examples.en: That shop stayed open late to bring in more money during the holiday.

explain: '벌다'보다 돈을 안으로 끌어오는 느낌이 강하고, 회사·나라·가게 이야기에 많이 나와요. 개인이 용돈이나 월급을 번다고 할 때는 그냥 '벌다'가 훨씬 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: The tourism industry brings in a lot of foreign currency.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나라나 회사가 돈을 크게 벌 때 같이 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when a country or company earns a lot of money.

phrases.en: They bought a new building with the money they earned.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 번 돈을 말할 때 '-ㄴ'을 붙여 명사 앞에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The -ㄴ form before a noun refers to money already earned.

phrases.en: I earn pocket money from a part-time job.
phrases.nuance_ko: 개인이 돈을 버는 일에는 '벌어들이다'보다 '벌다'가 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: For individuals earning money, 벌다 sounds more natural than 벌어들이다.

explain_en: It has a stronger sense of bringing money in than plain '벌다', and it is common when talking about companies, countries and shops. For an individual earning pocket money or a salary, plain '벌다' is far more natural.

examples.en: A company has to pay corporate tax every year.

examples.ko: 정부가 내년부터 법인세 인하를 추진한다고 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced it will push for a corporate tax cut starting next year.

examples.ko: 법인세 신고 기간이 다가와서 회계팀이 바빠요.
examples.en: The accounting team is busy because the corporate tax filing period is coming up.

examples.ko: 법인세는 개인이 아니라 회사가 내는 세금이에요.
examples.en: Corporate tax is paid by companies, not individuals.
The more profit there is, the more corporate tax increases.
Opinions are split over the corporate tax rate.

explain: 개인이 소득에 내는 세금은 '소득세', 회사 같은 법인이 내는 세금은 법인세예요. 뉴스에서는 '법인세 인하', '법인세율'처럼 자주 나와요. '세'로 끝나는 말이라 '세금'을 또 붙이지 않아도 돼요.

phrases.example: 이익이 나면 회사는 법인세를 내야 해요.
phrases.en: If a company makes a profit, it has to pay corporation tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금을 납부한다는 뜻으로 가장 기본적인 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic collocation for paying this tax.

phrases.example: 정부는 법인세 인하로 투자를 늘리겠다고 했어요.
phrases.en: The government said it would boost investment by cutting corporation tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 세금을 낮춘다는 소식에 자주 나오는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase often seen in news about tax cuts.

phrases.en: The corporation tax rate is different in each country.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금의 비율을 말할 때 쓰고, 경제 기사에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for the percentage rate of the tax; common in economic articles.

explain_en: Tax individuals pay on income is '소득세', while tax paid by corporations such as companies is 법인세. In the news it often appears as '법인세 인하' (corporate tax cut) and '법인세율' (rate). Since it already ends in '세', you don't need to add '세금' again.

examples.en: The exchange rate fluctuates every day.
The price changed depending on the weather.
The schedule might change.
It is a day when stock prices swing widely.
If the timetable changes, I will let you know.
Please check whether the number of attendees has changed.

explain: 가격, 수치, 일정이 오르내리거나 바뀔 때 써요. 명사 '변동'은 '가격 변동', '변동이 크다'처럼 나와요. '변하다'는 성격이나 사람에도 쓰지만 '변동하다'는 주로 숫자와 상황에 써요.

phrases.en: Stock prices fluctuate a lot these days.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '변동'과 함께 많이 바뀐다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The noun 변동 is used to say something changes a lot.

phrases.en: In summer, vegetable prices fluctuate a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가격이 오르내리는 것을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for prices going up and down.

phrases.example: 이 가격은 일 년 동안 변동하지 않아요.
phrases.en: This price doesn't change for a year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀌지 않는다고 말할 때 부정형으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form says something stays the same.

explain_en: It is used when prices, numbers, or schedules go up and down or shift. The noun appears in '가격 변동' (price fluctuation) and '변동이 크다' (big swings). '변하다' (to change) can describe a person or personality, but '변동하다' is mostly for figures and situations.

examples.en: How much is the luggage storage fee per day?
Please pay the storage fee all at once at the end of the month.
I paid the winter clothes storage fee in advance.
To save the storage fee, I decided to take it myself.
The storage fee also includes insurance.
I paid a thousand won as the locker fee.

explain: 짐이나 물건을 맡길 때 내는 돈이에요. 보통 '보관료를 내다', '보관료가 들다'처럼 써요. 비슷한 '보관비'도 쓰지만 가게나 서비스 안내에서는 '보관료'가 더 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: I left my bag and paid the storage fee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 지불한다는 가장 기본적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic phrase for paying the fee.

phrases.example: 큰 짐을 맡기면 보관료가 많이 들어요.
phrases.en: If you leave a large item, the storage fee is high.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비용이 생긴다는 뜻으로, 얼마나 드는지 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the cost is incurred; used when talking about how much it costs.

phrases.en: How much is the storage fee per month?
phrases.nuance_ko: '보관료'와 같은 뜻이지만 안내문에서는 '보관료'를 더 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 보관료, though signs more often use 보관료.

explain_en: It is the money you pay to leave luggage or goods for safekeeping, used as '보관료를 내다' or '보관료가 들다'. '보관비' is also used, but '보관료' is more common on shop and service notices.

examples.ko: 우리 회사는 특허를 열 개 보유해요.
examples.en: Our company holds ten patents.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 세계 기록을 보유하고 있어요.
examples.en: That athlete holds a world record.
The money the bank holds has dropped a lot.

examples.ko: 이 병원은 내년에 새 장비를 보유할 거예요.
examples.en: This hospital will have new equipment next year.

examples.ko: 예전에는 이 나라가 큰 군대를 보유했어요.
examples.en: This country used to maintain a large army.

examples.ko: 집을 두 채 보유해서 세금이 많아요.
examples.en: I own two houses, so my taxes are high.

explain: '가지다'는 아무 물건에나 쓰지만, '보유하다'는 회사·나라·단체가 기록, 재산, 기술 같은 것을 가지고 있을 때 써요. 뉴스와 서류에서 자주 보여요. 보통 '보유하고 있다'로 말해요.

phrases.example: 이 회사는 좋은 기술을 보유하고 있어요.
phrases.en: This company holds good technology.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지금 가지고 있는 상태를 말하는 가장 흔한 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common form, describing something currently held.

phrases.en: That athlete is a world record holder.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보유자'는 기록이나 자격을 가진 사람을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: 보유자 refers to a person who holds a record or qualification.

phrases.en: I have an old book.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 모든 물건에 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday word that works for any object.

explain_en: '가지다' works for any object, but '보유하다' is used when a company, country, or group holds records, assets, or technology. It shows up in news and documents. It is usually said as '보유하고 있다'.

examples.en: There was an accident, so I received insurance money.
The insurance payout will arrive within ten days.
You need documents to claim the insurance money.
I paid the hospital bill with insurance money.
I was surprised that the payout was smaller than I expected.
The insurance money was paid out to the family.

explain: 혼동하기 쉬운 말이 있어요. 매달 내는 돈은 '보험료', 사고나 병이 났을 때 받는 돈이 '보험금'이에요. '보험금을 받다/청구하다/지급하다'로 써요.

phrases.en: I received insurance money for the hospital bill.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사고나 병이 났을 때 돈을 받는 쪽에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the person who receives the money.

phrases.en: Yesterday I filed an insurance claim with the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 달라고 신청할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when applying for the payout.

phrases.en: The company paid out the insurance money.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 주는 회사 쪽에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used from the side of the company that pays.

explain_en: These two are easy to mix up. The money you pay every month is 보험료, and the money you receive after an accident or illness is 보험금. The verbs are 보험금을 받다, 청구하다 and 지급하다.

examples.en: Today's business just barely broke even.
With stocks, even breaking even is a relief.
I worked hard, but in the end I only broke even.

examples.ko: 이 게임은 해 봐야 본전치기일 거예요.
examples.en: Even if you try this game, you'll probably only break even.
It's a pity that it ended with just breaking even.
This month's event was close to breaking even as well.

explain: 이익도 손해도 없이 들인 돈만 겨우 건졌다는 뜻으로, 구어에서 자주 써요. '손해는 안 봤다'는 안도와 '남는 게 없다'는 아쉬움이 같이 있어요. '본전'은 처음에 들인 돈이에요.

phrases.example: 이번 달 장사도 겨우 본전치기를 했어요.
phrases.en: My business just broke even again this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '이다' 대신 '하다'를 붙여 본전치기의 결과를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Using '하다' instead of '이다' reports the result of breaking even.

phrases.example: 비싸게 샀지만 중고로 팔아서 본전을 건졌어요.
phrases.en: I bought it at a high price, but I got my money back by selling it used.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산 값만큼 다시 돌려받았다는 뜻이고, 본전치기와 비슷한 상황에 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: It means you got back what you paid, a situation similar to breaking even.

phrases.en: I worked hard, but in the end I only broke even.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거의 결과를 말하는 해요체이고 아쉬운 마음이 들어 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the polite past form, with a tone of mild disappointment.

explain_en: It is a colloquial word meaning you only just got back the money you put in, with no profit and no loss. It carries both relief at not losing and disappointment at gaining nothing. '본전' is the original money invested.

examples.en: Tax is added to the price.
New content was added to the explanation.

examples.ko: 기본 요금에 서비스 요금이 부가되는 가게도 있어요.
examples.en: Some stores add a service charge on top of the base price.

examples.ko: 이 상품에는 특별한 기능이 부가되어 있어요.
examples.en: This product comes with an extra feature added.

examples.ko: 점수에 보너스가 부가되면 순위가 달라질 거예요.
examples.en: If a bonus is added to the score, the ranking will change.
I marked the added items in red.

explain: 부가되다는 이미 있는 것 위에 따로 더해질 때 써요. '부가 가치세', '부가 서비스'처럼 앞에 붙는 말로도 자주 나와요. '추가되다'는 목록에 하나 더 들어가는 느낌이고, 부가되다는 본체에 딸려 붙는 느낌이에요.

phrases.en: It is convenient because it has many added features.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸미는 활용형으로 기본에 더해진 것을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A modifier form for things added on top of the basics.

phrases.en: A new dish was added to the menu.
phrases.nuance_ko: 목록에 하나 더 들어갈 때 써서 '부가되다'보다 일상적이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when one more item joins a list, and more everyday than '부가되다'.

phrases.en: A short note was tacked on to the explanation.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이미 있는 것 뒤에 붙는 느낌이 강한 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy word with a strong sense of being tacked on afterward.

explain_en: 부가되다 is used when something is added separately on top of what already exists. The form 부가 shows up in words like 부가 가치세 (VAT) and 부가 서비스. 추가되다 feels like one more item in a list, while 부가되다 feels like something attached to the main thing.

examples.ko: 주말에 번역 일을 해서 부수입이 생겼어요.
examples.en: I did translation work on weekends and made some extra income.
Thanks to the side income, I saved up for the trip.
I wish I had some extra income besides my salary.
He earns a little side income from his blog.
I use the extra money to help with living expenses.

examples.ko: 용돈 벌이로 시작했는데 부수입이 꽤 커졌어요.
examples.en: It started as pocket money, but the side income has grown quite a bit.

explain: 본업의 월급 말고 따로 생기는 돈을 말해요. '부업'은 하는 일이고 '부수입'은 그 일로 번 돈이라서 달라요. '부수입이 생기다', '부수입을 올리다'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: I'm earning extra income from my blog.
phrases.nuance_ko: '부수입이 생기다'는 저절로 생긴 느낌이고, '올리다'는 내가 노력해서 번다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 부수입이 생기다 means it just came up; 올리다 means you actively earn it.

phrases.en: The extra income from my weekend part-time job is quite good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생각보다 꽤 괜찮은 금액이라는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the extra income is better than expected.

phrases.en: I got some pocket money from my extra income.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부수입을 어떻게 썼는지 말할 때 '으로'를 붙여서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Add 으로 to say what the extra income was used for.

explain_en: It is money that comes in apart from your main salary. '부업' is the side job itself, while '부수입' is the money you earn from it. It is used in phrases like '부수입이 생기다' and '부수입을 올리다'.

examples.en: The new product sold like hot cakes the moment it came out.
In cold winter, hand warmers sell like hot cakes at convenience stores.
The snacks sold out fast on the first day of the sale.

examples.ko: 불티나는 인기를 끈 장난감이 벌써 품절됐어요.
examples.en: The wildly popular toy is already sold out.
At lunchtime, boxed lunches sell like crazy.
It is a shame that the shop that used to sell so well has closed.

explain: 대부분 '불티나게 팔리다'처럼 상품이 아주 빠르게 팔리는 상황에 써요. 가게 광고나 뉴스에서 자주 쓰는 표현이고, 사람이 아니라 물건이 주어예요.

phrases.en: The new sneakers sold like hot cakes.
phrases.nuance_ko: '불티나다'가 가장 자주 쓰이는 기본 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: This is the most common basic form of '불티나다'.

phrases.en: What products are selling like hot cakes these days?
phrases.nuance_ko: 뒤의 명사를 꾸며 줄 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to modify the noun that follows.

phrases.en: The concert tickets sold out in no time.
phrases.nuance_ko: '팔려 나가다'를 붙이면 계속 팔리는 느낌이 더 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding '팔려 나가다' makes it feel like they keep selling one after another.

explain_en: It is mostly used as '불티나게 팔리다' for goods that sell very fast. It appears in shop ads and news, and the subject is a product, not a person.

examples.en: Designer bags are classified as luxury goods.

examples.ko: 사치품에 돈을 너무 많이 쓰지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't spend too much money on luxury goods.

examples.ko: 이 나라는 사치품에 세금을 많이 매겨요.
examples.en: This country puts heavy taxes on luxury goods.

examples.ko: 요즘은 시계도 사치품이 아니라 필수품이 됐어요.
examples.en: These days, even a watch is a necessity rather than a luxury.
It's better to save than to buy luxury goods.
In a recession, luxury goods sales drop.

explain: 꼭 필요하지 않은데 값이 비싼 물건에 쓰는 말이라서 '필수품'과 반대로 말해요. '명품'은 품질이 좋다는 긍정적인 느낌이 있지만, '사치품'은 분수에 넘친다는 느낌이 더 있어요. '사치'에 '-품'이 붙은 말이라서 '사치스럽다'와 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.en: I bought luxury goods as soon as I got my paycheck.
phrases.nuance_ko: 비싼 물건을 샀다는 말에 조금 부정적인 느낌이 있어요.
phrases.nuance_en: Carries a slightly negative feeling about buying expensive things.

phrases.example: 요즘 젊은 사람들의 사치품 소비가 늘었대요.
phrases.en: I heard luxury spending among young people has increased.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 경제 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing often used in news and economic talk.

phrases.en: In the past, people considered coffee a luxury.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 물건을 꼭 필요하지 않은 비싼 것으로 본다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means seeing something as an unnecessary expensive item.

explain_en: It is used for expensive items you don't really need, and it is the opposite of '필수품' (necessities). '명품' sounds positive about quality, while '사치품' carries more of a 'beyond your means' feeling. It is '사치' plus '-품', so it is worth learning together with '사치스럽다'.

en: to cut; to reduce; to curtail

examples.en: The city cut this year's culture budget.
The company said it would cut employees' pay.

examples.ko: 비용을 삭감하면 서비스가 나빠질 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you cut costs, the service may get worse.
The government is going to cut next year's subsidies.
We cut the advertising budget and decided to focus on online.
Where does the money from the cut budget go?

explain: 예산·월급·비용처럼 정해진 돈의 양을 줄일 때 써요. '줄이다'는 아무 때나 쓰지만 '삭감하다'는 윗선에서 결정해 깎는 느낌이라 뉴스와 회사 글에 많아요. 반대말은 '증액하다'예요.

phrases.en: This year's subsidy was cut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 줄어든 돈을 주어로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the money that got reduced is the subject.

phrases.en: The event was canceled because of the budget cut.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사로 써서 줄이는 일 자체를 말해요. 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used as a noun for the act of cutting itself. Common in the news.

phrases.en: The company decided not to cut salaries.
phrases.nuance_ko: 깎지 않는다는 결정을 부정형으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, for a decision not to cut.

explain_en: It is used when a fixed amount of money, such as a budget, pay or cost, is reduced. 줄이다 works in any situation, but 삭감하다 feels like a decision made from above, so it is common in news and company writing. The opposite is 증액하다.

examples.en: When I get paid for my work, I save it right away.

examples.ko: 삯도 못 받고 일한 일꾼들이 사장을 찾아왔어요.
examples.en: The workers who worked without being paid came to see the boss.

examples.ko: 짐을 옮겨 준 삯으로 오만 원을 드렸어요.
examples.en: I paid fifty thousand won for moving the luggage.

examples.ko: 삯이 너무 싸서 아무도 일하려 하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The pay was so low that nobody wanted to work.
I'll give you the pay on the day the work is finished.
The work is too hard for the pay.

explain: 일을 해 준 대가나 무언가를 쓰고 내는 돈을 말해요. 혼자 쓰면 옛날 말 같은 느낌이 있고, '뱃삯', '품삯' 같은 말 속에서 더 자주 보여요. 요즘 일상에서 월급은 '월급', 일당은 '일당'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I worked a day and got paid.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일한 대가로 돈을 받는다는 뜻의 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation meaning to receive money for work done.

phrases.en: How much is the ferry fare to the island?
phrases.nuance_ko: 배를 타고 내는 돈이고 '삯'이 들어간 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The fee paid for riding a boat, a common word containing 삯.

phrases.en: I helped with farm work and received my wages.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일한 시간이나 노동의 값으로 받는 돈이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Money received as payment for labor or time worked.

explain_en: It means money paid for work or for using something. On its own it sounds somewhat old-fashioned and shows up more in words like '뱃삯' (boat fare) and '품삯' (labor pay). In modern daily life people say '월급' for salary and '일당' for daily wages.

examples.en: This year's rice output increased compared with last year.
They introduced new technology to increase output.

examples.ko: 광산의 금 산출량은 해마다 줄고 있어요.
examples.en: The mine's gold output is decreasing every year.

examples.ko: 가뭄 때문에 산출량에 큰 차이가 생겼어요.
examples.en: The drought caused a big difference in yield.

examples.ko: 산출량과 소비량이 맞지 않으면 가격이 흔들려요.
examples.en: If production and consumption don't match, prices fluctuate.

examples.ko: 산출량 통계는 정부 홈페이지에서 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: Output statistics can be seen on the government website.

explain: 농산물, 광물, 공업 제품처럼 생산해 낸 양을 말해요. 일상에서는 '생산량'이 더 흔하게 쓰이고, '산출량'은 경제 뉴스나 통계 자료에서 자주 나와요. 짝이 되는 말로 '소비량'이 있어요.

phrases.en: This year's potato production increased a lot.
phrases.nuance_ko: '산출량'과 비슷하지만 일상 대화에서는 '생산량'을 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to '산출량', but '생산량' is more common in everyday talk.

phrases.en: The yield dropped because it didn't rain.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생산한 양이 줄어든 것을 통계나 뉴스 느낌으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in a news or statistics tone when output decreases.

phrases.example: 이 공장의 연간 산출량은 십만 개예요.
phrases.en: This factory's annual output is one hundred thousand units.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 해 동안 만든 양을 말하는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A collocation for the amount produced in one year.

explain_en: It refers to the amount produced, such as crops, minerals or manufactured goods. '생산량' is more common in daily life, while '산출량' often appears in economic news and statistics. Its counterpart is '소비량' (amount consumed).

examples.en: This city has had well-developed commerce and industry since long ago.
It's a center of commerce and industry, so there are always lots of people.

examples.ko: 정부가 상공업을 키우려고 새 정책을 발표했어요.
examples.en: The government announced a new policy to grow commerce and industry.

examples.ko: 조선 후기에는 상공업에 종사하는 사람이 늘었어요.
examples.en: In the late Joseon period, more people worked in commerce and industry.

examples.ko: 농업보다 상공업이 더 중요한 나라도 많아요.
examples.en: In many countries, commerce and industry matter more than farming.

examples.ko: 상공업의 발달로 도시 인구가 빠르게 늘었어요.
examples.en: With the growth of commerce and industry, the city population rose quickly.

explain: 장사(상업)와 공장 일(공업)을 함께 묶어 말할 때 써요. 말할 때보다 뉴스나 역사·사회 수업에서 많이 나오고, '농업'과 짝지어 비교하는 경우가 많아요.

phrases.en: Busan is a commercial and industrial city with a port.
phrases.nuance_ko: 도시의 특징을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to describe the character of a city.

phrases.en: Commerce and industry developed near the river.
phrases.nuance_ko: 지역의 발전을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when talking about a region's development.

phrases.example: 이 나라는 농업과 상공업이 모두 중요해요.
phrases.en: In this country, both agriculture and commerce and industry are important.
phrases.nuance_ko: '농업'과 함께 비교할 때 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often appears in comparison with agriculture.

explain_en: It bundles trade (상업) and manufacturing (공업) together. It shows up more in news and history or social studies classes than in casual speech, and is often contrasted with '농업' (agriculture).

examples.ko: 올해 우리 회사의 매출이 예상을 상회했어요.
examples.en: This year our company's sales exceeded expectations.
Days with temperatures above the yearly average continue.

examples.ko: 수입이 지출을 상회하면 저축할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If income is above spending, you can save.

examples.ko: 이번 달 판매량이 목표를 상회할 거예요.
examples.en: This month's sales will exceed the target.
The number of participants is running above expectations.
My score didn't make it above the average.

explain: '넘다'보다 딱딱한 말이고, 숫자나 기준, 예상과 비교할 때 써요. 짝말은 '하회하다'(기준보다 낮다)예요. '예상을 상회하다'처럼 '을/를'과 함께 쓰고 뉴스나 경제 보고서에서 자주 봐요.

phrases.en: This result exceeded expectations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기대나 예상보다 더 좋을 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for results better than expected.

phrases.en: Today's temperature is above the seasonal average.
phrases.nuance_ko: '상회하다'와 뜻이 같고 조금 더 부드러운 우리말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 상회하다, a slightly softer native word.

phrases.en: The figures came out above the target.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'을 붙여 뒤의 숫자나 성적을 꾸밀 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The modifier form, used to describe numbers or scores.

explain_en: A stiffer word than 넘다, used when comparing to numbers, standards, or expectations. Its opposite is 하회하다 (to fall below). It takes 을/를 as in '예상을 상회하다' and is common in news and business reports.

examples.en: The main product of this village is apples.
Farmers sell their produce directly at the market.
The factory's products go out nationwide.
We check the quality of the products carefully.
The weather was good this year, so there was a large yield.

examples.ko: 지역 생산물을 쓰는 식당이 늘고 있어요.
examples.en: More restaurants are using locally produced goods.

explain: 공장이나 농장에서 만들어 낸 물건 전체를 가리키는 조금 딱딱한 말이에요. 가게에서 파는 물건은 '상품', 먹을 것은 '농산물'처럼 구체적으로 말하는 경우가 많아요. 뉴스나 보고서에서 더 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The factory released a new product.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생산물'과 비슷하지만 공장에서 만든 물건에 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 생산물 but used more for factory-made goods.

phrases.en: This region is famous for its farm products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 생산물 중에서 농사로 얻은 것만 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers only to the part of produce that comes from farming.

phrases.en: This country exports its products overseas.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스나 보고서에서 자주 쓰는 딱딱한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A formal pairing common in news and reports.

explain_en: A rather formal word for everything made at a factory or farm. For goods sold in a shop Koreans say 상품, and for farm goods 농산물, which are more specific. 생산물 appears more in news and reports.

examples.ko: 이 공장의 생산품은 외국으로 많이 팔려요.
examples.en: This factory's products are sold a lot overseas.
We sell our village's products at the market.

examples.ko: 생산품에 문제가 있으면 바로 알려 주세요.
examples.en: If there is a problem with the product, please tell us right away.

examples.ko: 이 생산품이 어느 나라에서 만들어졌는지 확인해요.
examples.en: I check which country this product was made in.
We made a gift set out of the products.
I compared the prices of our own products and imported products.

explain: '제품'은 만들어 낸 물건 전체를, '상품'은 팔려고 내놓은 물건을 말해요. 생산품은 어느 곳에서 만든 물건이라는 점을 말할 때 써요. 외국에서 들여온 물건은 '수입품'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 마을 사람들이 시장에서 마을 생산품을 팔아요.
phrases.en: The villagers sell the village's products at the market.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그곳에서 만든 물건을 판다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when selling goods made in that place.

phrases.en: This store sells only local products.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그 지역에서 만든 물건을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to goods made in the local area.

phrases.en: This company's products are of good quality.
phrases.nuance_ko: '생산품'은 어디서 만들었는지를 강조하고, '제품'은 일상에서 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: 생산품 stresses where something was made, while 제품 is the more common everyday word.

explain_en: '제품' is any manufactured item and '상품' is an item put out for sale. 생산품 is used to say an item was made at a certain place. Goods brought in from abroad are '수입품'.

examples.en: In Japan you pay consumption tax when you buy things.
Opinions were divided over the consumption tax increase.
When the consumption tax rate rises, people tighten their wallets.
Consumption tax is included in this price.
Prices went up because of the consumption tax.

examples.ko: 일본 여행 때 외국인은 소비세 환급을 받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: When traveling in Japan, foreigners can get a consumption tax refund.

explain: 물건이나 서비스를 살 때 가격에 붙는 세금을 말해요. 한국에서 가격에 붙는 세금은 보통 '부가가치세'(부가세)라고 하고, '소비세'는 일본 등 다른 나라 뉴스에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: The government raised the consumption tax.
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금 비율이 높아질 때 '올리다'와 같이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with '올리다' when the tax rate goes up.

phrases.en: Consumption tax is added to this price.
phrases.nuance_ko: 가격 위에 세금이 더해진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the tax is added on top of the price.

phrases.en: The price includes VAT.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한국에서는 '소비세'보다 '부가세'를 일상에서 더 많이 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In Korea, 부가세 is used more often than 소비세 in daily life.

explain_en: It means the tax added to the price when you buy goods or services. In Korea the tax added to prices is usually called '부가가치세' (부가세), while '소비세' often appears in news about Japan and other countries.

examples.en: Prices rose slightly this month.
The stock price fell slightly and then recovered.
I saw news that the exchange rate rose slightly.
My score went up slightly from last time.
The temperature dropped a little, so the mornings are chilly.
My salary was raised slightly this year.

explain: 뉴스나 경제 기사에서 오르다, 내리다, 상승하다, 하락하다 앞에 자주 붙어요. 반대말은 '대폭'이에요. 일상 대화에서는 '조금'이나 '약간'이 더 편해요.

phrases.en: Gas prices rose slightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소폭 오르다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스나 기사에서 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A more formal version of 'rise slightly', common in news and articles.

phrases.en: The exchange rate fell slightly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 수치가 조금 내려갔을 때 쓰는 기사체 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A news-style phrase used when a figure drops by a small amount.

phrases.en: My pay went up a little this month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '소폭'과 같은 뜻이지만 일상 대화에서 더 편하게 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means the same as 'sopok' but is the everyday word in conversation.

explain_en: It often sits before verbs like 오르다, 내리다, 상승하다 and 하락하다 in news and economic articles. The opposite is '대폭'. In daily conversation, '조금' or '약간' feels more natural.

examples.en: How much did you actually receive this month?
After taxes, the amount you receive drops a lot too.

examples.ko: 보험금 수령액을 미리 계산해 볼 수 있어요.
examples.en: You can calculate the insurance payout in advance.
Check just the amount of salary you receive separately.
Your lifestyle changes depending on the pension you receive.
You get a text message when the amount is deposited.

explain: 받는 사람 입장에서 말하는 금액이에요. 주는 쪽에서는 '지급액'이라고 하고, 일상 대화에서는 '받는 돈'이라고도 해요.

phrases.en: How much is your take-home pay?
phrases.nuance_ko: 세금 등을 빼고 실제로 받는 돈을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The actual amount received after taxes and deductions.

phrases.en: Please check the amount the company has set to pay.
phrases.nuance_ko: 주는 쪽에서 보는 금액이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The amount seen from the paying side.

phrases.en: The amount I received went up a bit this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 돈이 많아지거나 적어질 때 '늘다/줄다'와 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Pair with 늘다/줄다 for increases or decreases.

explain_en: It is the amount from the receiver's point of view. The paying side calls it '지급액', and in casual talk people also say '받는 돈'.
